A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPOIL research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. V4 adds Appendices B.8–B.9 while retaining the subsequent appendices.

before.justification: V3 reports original experiments on generated linear MDPs and CartPole, Acrobot, and LunarLander, including additional comparisons in Appendix E.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same objective, critic best response, policy updates, and output selection. The convex-hull and finite-class additions provide new analyses of the existing algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same generated linear MDP scenarios and CartPole-v1, Acrobot-v1, and LunarLander-v2. The simple-expert, complex-expert, and redundant-feature scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: BC in Figures 1 and 4; BC, IQ-Learn, and P2IL in Figure 2; and BC and IQ-Learn in Figure 5.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same stated settings, including the linear MDP with 500 states, 1,000 actions, and seven features; trajectory subsampling every 20 or five steps; and evaluation of the best policy found. No substantive protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the redundant-feature example favoring BC, the linear IQ-Learn comparison, and the check against BC underoptimization. No new empirical ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 5 still report averages over 10 seeds, with unchanged plotted uncertainty bands. No empirical uncertainty-reporting practice changes; the concentration-bound revisions concern theory.

E6.justification: The empirical plots in Figures 1, 2, 4, and 5 retain identical data and findings. This includes SPOIL's advantage over BC for complex experts and the appendix example favoring BC. No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: New Appendices B.8–B.9 establish a convex-class guarantee with an ε^-2 accuracy factor, a convex-hull corollary, and a finite-class bound with linear dependence on class size. V4 also adds a uniform candidate-value bound to Assumption 1, corrects Hoeffding and concentration constants, repairs the linear covering argument, and revises general covering radii and associated derivations. These substantially extend and revise the theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal SPOIL contributions remain stable. Section 6 now claims a proved improvement for convex Q classes, whereas v3 presented improving the general ε^-4 rate entirely as future work.

C2.justification: V4 qualifies the remaining rate question for nonconvex classes. New Remarks 1–2 explain that convex-hull complexity can worsen the bound and that the finite-class result trades better accuracy dependence for worse class-size dependence. Existing practical limitations remain.

D1.justification: The network architectures, Adam settings, learning rate, shared Soft DQN updates, and code and expert-data access information are retained. Appendix E.3 corrects its Figure 5 reference to Figure 2 without changing the documented implementation details.

R1.justification: V4 adds Vershynin (2018) as a source for concentration and covering tools. Positioning relative to BC, IQ-Learn, AdVIL, and classical imitation learning remains stable; most other reference changes update metadata or citation formatting.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are retained, with local wording, terminology, proof-exposition, and cross-reference corrections. Two appendix subsections are added. Bibliographic formatting changes extensively, but v4 also replaces the Simchowitz et al. title with the placeholder 'The title of the paper'.

P2.justification: Figure 3's caption moves below its plot, other captions receive small edits, and pages reflow around the expanded appendix. The five figures, algorithm boxes, and Table 1 retain their basic display structure.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens the paper's central theoretical contribution: it partially resolves v3's open rate question through the convex-class result, supplies alternative guarantees, and corrects concrete concentration and covering-proof errors. The added boundedness assumption restricts the stated linear setting but makes a needed condition explicit. The new bounds' complexity tradeoffs are acknowledged. These gains outweigh the minor bibliographic regression; empirical evidence remains unchanged.
